gaps.sentence: If you want a refund, you ___ keep the receipt — no receipt, no refund.
gaps.hint: a necessity that applies in the future
gaps.explanation: Future necessity uses 'will have to': will have to keep.

gaps.sentence: You ___ to be more careful with your passwords.
gaps.explanation: 'Ought to' behaves like 'should' and always takes 'to': ought to be.

gaps.sentence: Luckily I ___ find a parking space right outside the theatre.
gaps.hint: one particular success on that occasion
gaps.explanation: One particular success takes 'was able to': was able to find.

gaps.sentence: When I was a child, I ___ stay up late on New Year's Eve.
gaps.hint: permission that existed in the past
gaps.explanation: 'Was allowed to' expresses past permission; 'could' is also possible: was allowed to.

gaps.sentence: Library books ___ be taken out of the reading room.
gaps.hint: a passive prohibition with mustn't be
gaps.explanation: Prohibitions can be passive: mustn't be taken.

gaps.sentence: He ___ not agree, but let us ask him anyway.
gaps.explanation: 'May' expresses a possibility about the future: may not agree.

gaps.sentence: The ground is wet, so it ___ have rained overnight.
gaps.explanation: 'Must have' plus the participle draws a certain conclusion about the past: must have rained.

gaps.sentence: You ___ as well tell him the truth — he will find out anyway.
gaps.explanation: 'Might as well' suggests doing something because there is no reason not to: might as well.
